title: Toward a More Complex Understanding of Natal Super Star Clusters with Multiwavelength Observations
question: Disentangle individual natal super star clusters in He 2-10 at ~0.3'' resolution using multiwavelength radio, submillimeter, and infrared observations to assess their ionizing photon rates, extinction, masses, and star formation efficiencies.

what.value: 1995 VLA AK0400 FITS images at 5, 8, and 15 GHz for flux calibration comparison

evidence.loc: Source Extraction and Photometry
evidence.quote: As a check, we convolved the 5, 8, and 15 GHz maps from programs AJ314 and 16B-067 to the synthesized beam from (cite: Johnson:2003) to compare the flux calibrations against their 1995 AK0400 program.

evidence.loc: Source Extraction and Photometry
evidence.quote: We are in possession of the original FITS images used in (cite: Johnson:2003) and are able to make a direct comparison without needing to re-reduce the data from the archive.

evidence.loc: Discussion
evidence.quote: and the white contours show ([7](#fig:normpar)a) SMA $^{12}$CO(2-1), ([7](#fig:normpar)b) ALMA HCO$^+$(1-0), and ([7](#fig:normpar)c) ALMA HCN(1-0) velocity-integrated intensity (moment 0) maps from (cite: Johnson:2018).

evidence.quote: (cite: Johnson:2018) report HCN(1-0), HCO$^+$(1-0), and CO(2-1) line strengths for nineteen 0.8$''$ apertures, chosen to probe peaks in their ALMA and SMA maps of He 2-10.

evidence.quote: This is motivated by the results of (cite: Cresci:2017), who mapped the metallicity of He 2-10 from their MUSE (Multi Unit Spectroscopic Explorer) observations. They report a range of metallicities (12 + log(O/H) = 8.25 – 8.55) across He 2-10

what.value: HCN/HCO+ and HCO+/CO molecular line ratio diagram data for comparison

evidence.loc: Discussion
evidence.quote: In Figure [8](#fig:molratios), we show an adaptation of Figure 13 from (cite: Johnson:2018) and Figure 13 of (cite: Finn:2019) to show this trend.

recipe.goal: Convolve radio/mm/submm maps to a common beam, stack them to define source apertures, and extract multiwavelength continuum and Pa-alpha photometry
recipe.method: Convolve all VLA and ALMA maps to a 0.3'' circular beam, stack the 8 convolved maps, define source footprints using the 20-sigma (73 uJy/bm) contour of the stacked map with manual masking in crowded regions, sum intensity divided by beam area, subtract median masked background; for HST/NICMOS Pa-alpha, shift by 1.33'', scale F187N by 3% and subtract F190N, and extract using the 33 GHz half-light radius contour (~2-sigma) with local background annuli.
key_parameters: Stacked map contour level = 20 x rms (73 uJy bm^-1)
Pa-alpha background annulus = 1.5 to 2 times source size (2 to 3 times for Knot 4b)
assumptions: Rayleigh-Jeans tail of hot star SEDs makes continuum in F187N 3% brighter than in F190N
Systematic flux calibration errors: 10% for ALMA, 5% for VLA < 15 GHz, 15% for VLA >= 15 GHz

recipe.goal: Fit 2-component and 3-component power-law SED models to disentangle non-thermal, free-free, and dust emission
recipe.method: Fit log S_model = log(S_0,nth nu^alpha_nth + S_0,ff nu^alpha_ff + S_0,dust nu^alpha_dust) via chi-squared minimization with fixed spectral indices, excluding the 33 GHz lower limit and modifying the 5 GHz and 15 GHz fluxes and uncertainties to account for archival calibration discrepancies.
key_parameters: 5 GHz flux modified to midpoint between Table 4 value and 0.5x value; 15 GHz flux modified to midpoint between Table 4 value and 1.4x value
assumptions: Free-free emission is optically thin above 5 GHz (alpha_ff = -0.1) and dust emission is optically thin (alpha_dust = 4)

recipe.goal: Estimate ionizing photon production rates (Q_Lyc), cluster stellar masses (M_fit), and visual extinction (A_V)
recipe.method: Calculate Q_Lyc,fit from the SED-modeled 33 GHz thermal flux density (S_ff,fit) using Equation (2); convert Q_Lyc,fit to cluster stellar mass M_fit using Starburst99 models; calculate Q_Lyc,Pa-alpha from HST/NICMOS Pa-alpha flux density using Equations (2)-(4); derive extinction A_V = -17.7 log(Q_Lyc,Pa-alpha / Q_Lyc,fit).
key_parameters: T_e = 10^4 K, nu = 33 GHz, D = 9 Mpc
Starburst99 conversion: Q_Lyc = (5.3 +/- 1.2) x 10^52 photons s^-1 per 10^6 M_sun cluster (< 1 Myr, Z = 0.008 and 0.014, Kroupa and Salpeter IMFs)
F(Pa-alpha) / F(H-beta) = 0.317, F187N FWHM = 0.0191 um, A_Pa-alpha / A_K ~ 1.24, A_V / A_K ~ 8.8 (R_V = 3.1)
assumptions: T_e = 10^4 K, Case B recombination, n_e = 10^6 cm^-3, cluster age < 1 Myr, optically thin free-free emission, R_V = 3.1

recipe.goal: Calculate dust masses, gas masses, total cluster masses, and instantaneous mass ratios (star formation efficiencies)
recipe.method: Use SED-modeled 340 GHz dust flux density (S_dust,fit) to compute dust mass M_d = L_nu / (4 pi kappa_nu B_nu(T_d)) for T_d = (25, 40, 100) K; multiply by gas-to-dust ratio to get M_gas, add M_fit for total mass, and compute instantaneous mass ratio IMR(t) = (1 + M_* / M_gas)^-1 (or SFE).
key_parameters: T_d = (25, 40, 100) K; nu_0 = 340 GHz; kappa_0 = 1.3 cm^2 g^-1; beta = alpha_dust - 2 = 2
assumptions: Optically thin dust emission at 340 GHz, kappa_0 = 1.3 cm^2 g^-1 at 340 GHz, T_d = (25, 40, 100) K, dust-to-gas ratio of 1:100

score_reason: All ALMA, VLA, and HST data are in public archives, the SED fitting equations and analytic formulas for Q_Lyc, A_V, M_d, and SFE are explicitly given, and the intermediate photometry is tabulated in Table 4. However, full end-to-end reproduction from visibilities is hindered by unstated tclean imaging parameters, unstated continuum channel selections, and manual pixel masking of crowded contours.
rediscovery_reason: All datasets are public in the ALMA, VLA, and HST archives, the main deliverables are numeric (continuum flux densities, SED component amplitudes, ionizing photon rates, stellar/dust masses, A_V, and SFE), and downstream reproduction from the tabulated photometry in Table 4 is completely specified.
